chunks: Reclining in it on couches, they will see in it neither the sun nor intense cold.

key_terms.الْأَرَائِكِ: Raised couches or beds with cushions

ai.seo_question: What does the Quran say about the comfort of the people of Paradise regarding sun and cold?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, 'al-arā'ik' (raised couches) signifies not merely physical comfort but a state of dignified repose and spiritual elevation, free from the servitude of worldly toil. The absence of 'shams' (intense, oppressive heat) and 'zamharir' (biting cold) symbolizes the removal of both external hardships and internal spiritual extremes, reflecting the divine balance (mizan) that characterizes the abode of the righteous.
